candidates.title: Good Morning

connections.analysis: Interpretive comparison: Ozu's conflict over speech and silence offers a different test of communication from Tati's largely wordless social choreography. These catalog descriptions support the comparison, not a claim of identical sound design.

Interpretive comparison: both distributor descriptions locate comedy in ordinary social behavior shaped by consumer modernity. This is a modest candidate link to a fictional high rating, not evidence of shared authorial intent or guaranteed appeal.

candidates.productiveDifference: The sources place Ozu's comedy in a suburban family and neighborhood, rather than Tati's choreographed traversal of modern Paris. No matching lens, camera, or production technique is asserted.

candidates.title: Syndromes and a Century

connections.analysis: Interpretive comparison: the director's account of memory and repeated situations offers another way to question a single authoritative narrative, alongside the documented reality and reenactment interplay in Close-Up. The sources do not establish direct influence.

Interpretive comparison: the director's contrast between two hospital settings invites attention to how built environments organize experience. Tati's documented modern-Paris setting provides a second spatial anchor, without implying the same comic tone or camera grammar.

candidates.productiveDifference: The official interview centers family memory and repeated hospital situations; this differs from Tati's social comedy and Kiarostami's documented case. The fictional middling Tropical Malady rating also cautions against inferring universal enthusiasm for this director.
